2840: The king is down and the royal guard carried him to the rear — command from the overview.
2841: Battles led by a general are commanded from the overview.
2843: The chancellor gathers craftsmen to upgrade arms, armor, drill and supply. One at a time and it takes days, but it applies to every soldier forever.
2844: Realm → Upgrades tab. Start with Better arms (attack +6%)
2846: On day 20 a Great Raid hits the Palace. Each wall level cuts our losses in defense by 12%, and archers shoot down from the walls.
2849: Drill a ★★ company for 7 more days and it becomes elite — Elite Infantry, Spearmen, Archers, Cavalry. Expensive and slow, but they turn battles.
2850: Drill a company twice (★★), then Realm → Garrison tab → Make elite (gold 700 · food 250)
2852: While a fort stands, the Dead keep coming. Scout its deployment with spies, build an army that counters it, and start with the nearest fort, Morgash.
2853: March → pick the fort → choose general and troops. Stronger if the king goes in person
2854: Use a general's skill in battle
2855: Each general has a unique skill — the King's Roar (morale), Eorin's charge, Hadrik's shield wall… one move that turns the tide.
2856: Q in battle (or the skill button at the bottom). Has a cooldown
2858: The king is a body you move yourself. The Dead won't come for the first 7 days, so learn your way around the castle.
2859: Walk around the castle and look at the buildings
2860: WASD move · Shift run · Alt switches between view mode (turn with mouse) and cursor mode · E at a building opens the door
2862: Higher prowess raises the king's HP and damage. The longer the king lasts on the field, the more his soldiers' morale holds.
2863: Cut the dummies at the southwest training yard (right-click) — follow the yellow dotted line on the ground. Chain hits to gain more
2864: Open the map at the war table
2865: The whole realm is ruled from the map. Villages, forts and neighboring realms are there.
2866: At the table in front of the Great Hall, E, or M. M again to come back
2867: Enter the Great Hall and meet your ministers
2868: Inside the Great Hall are the ministers who run the realm: Chancellor (building, recruiting), Treasurer (taxes), Spymaster (spies), High Priest (blessings), Chamberlain (petitions), the war council table, the wardrobe, and the generals.
2869: Walk in through the Great Hall's big doors. E in front of a minister. The chamberlain collects the people's petitions (audiences) — E in front of him, or sit on the throne, to hear them
2871: Taxes balance gold against favor. Early on, protecting favor makes the population grow faster.
2872: In the Great Hall, Treasurer Bella on the right, E → Tax policy
2874: Building levels drive recruiting speed, taxes, food and population. Spare gold goes here first.
2875: 'Realm' below → Build. Start with farms (food), market (gold), housing (people)
2877: The garrison is the Palace's shield. Training takes days, so recruit before the attack comes.
2878: At the barracks door (E) or Realm → Recruit. Mix infantry, spearmen and archers
2880: The world doesn't sit still. Merchants, refugees, scouts, wolves… when an event comes, the game pauses and asks you to choose. For events that need an army, 'View on map' takes you to the map to pick one. If it's not urgent, defer it with 'Hear it a day later'.
2881: Fishermen will come by shortly. Just pick an option
2883: Fresh companies are weak. Drilling earns ★ for attack and defense, and at ★★ you can raise them into elites (infantry, spearmen, archers, cavalry).
2884: Realm → Recruit tab → 'Drill companies' list, drill one company (gold 70 · food 30 · 2 days). Also at the barracks door (E). Elite training is in the Garrison tab
2886: Village population drives taxes, food and village recruiting. Mines and toll houses add gold every day.
2887: Click the gold-blinking mine or riverside village → Manage village → Mine expansion/Toll house. Village recruiting or walls work too
2888: Send a garrison to a village
2889: The Dead besiege the farthest villages first. A garrison holds out days longer and buys time for relief.
2890: On the map, village → Send garrison (detached from the Palace garrison)
2891: Send a spy to a fort
2892: Knowing the enemy's numbers and units lets you build an army that counters them.
2893: Click the fort Morgash in the north of the map (visible from the start) → Spy. Click a '?' in the fog and send a spy to find out what it is
2894: Send an envoy to a neighboring realm
2895: At relations 40: trade and treaties; at 70: borrow reinforcements. Envoys cost no gold.
2896: On the map, click a neighbor's capital → Send envoy. Once every 5 days
2897: Spar with a general at the Colosseum
2898: Sparring raises both prowess and the general's experience, and pays gold.
2899: At the west Colosseum door, E → pick a general. Finish one bout (win or lose) to pass. Your opponent scales to the king's prowess
2900: First week's guide complete. Now go after the forts of the Dead.
2901: Second week's guide complete. The realm is in your hands now.
2902: Today is the last day to prepare — the Dead move from tomorrow. The guide disappears tonight.
